extract:
Michael Jackson was born on August 29, 1958, in Gary, Indiana, the eighth of ten children in a working-class family. His recording career ran from the late 1960s until his death in Los Angeles on June 25, 2009, and his estate continued to issue posthumous material into the following decade. He first came to prominence as the lead singer of the Jackson 5, a family group his father Joseph Jackson managed. The group played the Midwestern talent-show and chitlin' circuit before signing to Berry Gordy's Motown Records in 1968.

His formative influences came from that circuit's soul showmen, above all James Brown and Jackie Wilson, whose footwork and vocal attack he studied from the wings. At Motown he absorbed the label's polished production discipline. While the Jackson 5 scored hits such as "I Want You Back" and "ABC," Motown launched him as a solo act with Got To Be There in 1972, whose title track was a hit. That same year came Ben, whose title song, the theme from the film of the same name, became his first solo number one in the US. Music & Me (1973) and Forever, Michael (1975) followed, the latter featuring "One Day in Your Life." These albums leaned on sweet soul balladry and gave him limited creative control.

The decisive break came after the brothers moved to Epic Records. Working with Quincy Jones, whom he met on the set of The Wiz, Jackson released Off the Wall in 1979. The album fused disco, funk and R&B on tracks like "Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough" and "Rock with You," the latter written by Rod Temperton. Jones and engineer Bruce Swedien returned for Thriller (1982), which became the best-selling album of all time. Its singles included "Billie Jean," "Beat It" with an Eddie Van Halen guitar solo, "Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'," "Thriller" with a Vincent Price narration, and "The Girl Is Mine" with Paul McCartney. Bad (1987), the final Jones collaboration, produced a run of number-one singles including "Man in the Mirror" and "Smooth Criminal." Dangerous (1991) shifted toward new jack swing with producer Teddy Riley on "Remember the Time" and "Jam." HIStory (1995) paired a hits disc with new songs such as "Scream," a duet with his sister Janet Jackson, and "Earth Song," with production from Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis. Blood on the Dance Floor (1997) collected remixes, and Invincible (2001), made with Rodney Jerkins, was his final studio album.

His cultural footprint is difficult to overstate. The "Billie Jean" and "Beat It" videos helped break MTV's color barrier, and John Landis's "Thriller" short film redefined the music video as an event. His moonwalk on the 1983 Motown 25 broadcast became one of television's most famous performances. Thriller won a record eight Grammys in 1984, and he co-wrote "We Are the World" with Lionel Richie in 1985. His later years were overshadowed by child sexual abuse allegations, including a 2005 criminal trial that ended in acquittal. Those allegations continue to complicate how his work is received.

Jackson died in 2009 while rehearsing for the This Is It concert residency in London. Epic and his estate have since issued Thriller 25 (2008), the posthumous compilation Michael (2010), Bad 25 (2012), and XSCAPE (2014), on which L.A. Reid and Timbaland reworked unreleased recordings, including "Love Never Felt So Good." His estate has also backed the stage musical MJ, keeping his catalog among the most commercially active in pop history.
title: Michael Jackson
